engineering.title: BVEX — Balloon-Borne Very-Small-Baseline Interferometer
engineering.role: Electronics & Software Lead · Queen's Physics · Summer 2025

cover.alt: Stratospheric balloon being inflated on the Timmins runway at sunset, with the BVEX payload gondola visible

description: Designed and built the electronics systems for a balloon-borne radio telescope that flew to 15 km altitude during a CSA/CNES campaign in Timmins, Ontario. Responsible for power distribution, thermal regulation, and inertial position tracking using LabJack T7 DAQs, relay boards, accelerometers, gyroscopes, and Raspberry Pi 5.

Wrote multithreaded C software with UDP servers to control relays, stream telemetry at 1 kHz, and maintain payload temperature within ±2°C. Co-authored two SPIE conference papers on the telescope design and its RFSoC digital backend.

engineering.title: Autonomous RC Car — "Town of Quackston"

cover.alt: Team of four holding the PiCar-X at the Quackston competition, with the course map displayed behind them

description: Built a PiCar-X into an autonomous taxi that could keep its lane, take turns, stop, and signal, while navigating a simulated city block to pick up and drop off passengers for fares.

Owned the control subsystem: a hand-tuned PID controller for lane-keeping, plus a Coral TPU-assisted trajectory follower using a bicycle steering model for camera-guided turns, with a pivot-turn fallback whenever camera guidance was lost.

Designed the mission state machine governing high-level driving behaviour and wired turn signals and brake lights over GPIO. Subsystems communicated over a ZeroMQ publish–subscribe architecture shared with the perception and planning teams.

engineering.title: Smith Hyperloop — Tunnel Boring Machine

cover.alt: Smith Hyperloop Tunnel Boring Machine Team

description: Led the electrical team designing and testing power distribution and navigation-control systems for a tunnel boring machine built for an international tunnelling competition. Designed four electrical subsystems: a 480 VAC three-phase power path with fused disconnect, dual contactors, and VFD-driven cutter motor; a 120 VAC auger motor branch; a dual-channel safety relay system with E-stop; and a Teensy/Raspberry Pi embedded controls platform with isolated ADC current sensing and RS-485 VFD communication.
Coordinated deliverables across the mechanical, software, and electrical subteams to keep integration on track under competition deadlines.

engineering.title: MOSFET Device Design & Simulation

Simulated all device parameters and produced a professional datasheet with I-V characteristics, capacitance curves, and process parameters.

engineering.title: Walking vs. Jumping ML Classifier
description: Built a machine learning model to classify accelerometer data as walking or jumping using feature extraction (FFT, RMS, peak frequency) and scikit-learn classifiers. Collected real sensor data, trained and evaluated multiple models, and documented the full pipeline from data collection through cross-validated accuracy analysis.

engineering.title: Digital Student Card System

cover.alt: Digital student card prototype setup with smartphone running digital pass in Apple Wallet, USB QR scanner, and Java desktop portal

description: Developed a digital student card system for Queen's University designed to replace physical plastic cards, enabling students to seamlessly use their smartphone for dining hall meals, TAMs (Trade A Meal), Flex dollars, and athletics facility (ARC) access.
Engineered a fully functional prototype comprising a Java Swing desktop front-end, CSV database, and dedicated hardware QR scanner for rapid student identification and transaction authorization.
Implemented secure data handling, encryption protocols, and input validation logic while adhering to a $100 prototype budget constraint and outlining a complete full-scale campus implementation plan.

engineering.title: Generative Music AI's $350M Problem
engineering.role: QMIND AI Ethics Team · Oct 2024 – May 2025
description: Researched how generative AI reshapes copyright and creator compensation in the music industry as part of a 5-person QMIND research team, evaluating federated learning, digital watermarking, and audio fingerprinting as possible safeguards.
Co-authored the resulting paper and presented findings at CUCAI, Canada's largest undergraduate AI conference.
